title: Introduce client-driven backpressure tokens and staggered partial-output reclamation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: when clients disconnect mid-generation or become slow, the server's aggressive reclamation of partial outputs causes synchronized GC spikes, lost tool-call state, and surprising resume behavior for long-lived sessions. This ticket designs and implements a client-driven token mechanism and a staggered reclamation policy to reduce contention, preserve partial tool/function-call invariants for a bounded window, and make behavior compatible across older SDKs and newer runtimes.

Goals:
1) Let clients optionally advertise consumption capacity using lightweight backpressure tokens (consumption credits) so the server can pace emission without holding long-lived in-memory partials indefinitely.
2) Introduce a staggered, priority-driven partial-output reclamation sweeper that avoids mass eviction storms and preserves tool-call side effects long enough for typical reconnects.
3) Ensure function/tool calling remains atomic and observable even when partial outputs are reclaimed (no duplicated tool invocations on resume).
4) Maintain compatibility modes: strict-compat (current behavior), token-aware (new behavior), and legacy-fallback for older SDKs.

Scope: runtime server, HTTP/SDK contract changes, SDK client (JS/Python) shim, console telemetry and incident alerts, e2e test harness for disconnect/timeouts and function-call idempotency.
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts optional backpressure token header and exposes credit counter in streaming metadata
Clients can request lease extension via heartbeat RPC or token refresh without blocking generation progress
Partial-output sweeper performs staggered reclamation across shards and reports per-tenant reclaimed ranges to the console
Tool/function calls that started but did not finish preserve an idempotency marker for at least the configurable hold window (default 2 minutes)
Older SDKs that do not send tokens continue to get previous behavior via legacy-fallback configuration
Regression tests covering disconnect-resume, timeout-triggered reclamation, and tool-call deduplication pass in CI
Telemetry dashboards show reduced peak reclaim rate and stable latency under simulated client disconnect bursts
notes: RFC note: opted for short lived client tokens (30s TTL) to avoid long server-side state and to make token refresh cheap for mobile clients
Telemetry: emit reclaim_reason labels (disconnect, timeout, memory-pressure, admin-manual) to distinguish causes
Config knobs: reclaim_stagger_window_ms, token_default_ttl_ms, tool_call_hold_window_ms configurable per-tenant
comments: 2026-01-15 Maya Chen: Created ticket after on-call postmortem (INC-2026-01) showed two reclamation storms correlated with an SDK bug that prevented backpressure signals from reaching the runtime.

2026-01-22 Arjun Patel: Implemented prototype of token header parsing and a lightweight counter in the connection state. Initial microbench shows 1.8% added p99 latency for very short generations; acceptable trade-off.

2026-01-28 Design review (Lydia Park): Agreed on stagger windows and prioritization tiers (active-resume, function-call-hold, ephemeral-prefix) — Lydia requested clearer invariant on tool-call idempotency and explicit test vectors.

2026-02-02 QA (Ravi Kumar): Wrote e2e harness that simulates 10k clients disconnecting randomly; observed 40% reduction in reclaimed objects per sweep after staggering. Caveat: memory pressure path still spikes if reclaim_stagger_window_ms too small.
2026-02-06 Security (Anya Rodriguez): Reviewed idempotency markers. Recommend HMAC over shard+generation id for marker authenticity; added note to design doc and a follow-up task for KMS integration.

2026-02-10 Arjun Patel: Opened runtime PR with sweep scheduler and token support. Next: make console dashboards surface reclaim hot spots and wire an alert for reclaim_rate > threshold. Moving to In Progress->In Review for SDK shims next week.
